h1: AI Lifestyle Photos for Wellness Brands, Set in a Real Routine
lead: A buyer recognizes the bottle when it sits next to a breakfast bowl she already owns. Upload that bottle and an AI avatar can set it on the table.
card: Routine photos and short clips for supplements, tea, and gear.

faq.q: Can the photo or clip show what a supplement does?
faq.a: No. Show how and when it is used, not a health result. Keep claims and dosage in text your team approves.

faq.q: Why does the label look washed out?
faq.a: Shoot the bottle upright, front label centered, with soft side light instead of a direct flash. Glare usually starts in that source photo.

faq.q: Can I use these in paid wellness ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloads have no watermark, so you can use them in paid ads. Any health claim or offer you add has to be accurate.

faq.q: Do I need a model or a creator?
faq.a: No. Pick an AI avatar. The clip can include a spoken line and captions. Hire a real person only when you need a true customer story.

faq.q: Can I make a Story from this?
faq.a: Yes. A square photo fits a feed or a product page. For a phone Story, make a tall clip at 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds.

A 6-second clip spends 24 credits, 10 seconds spends 40, 15 seconds spends 60, and 30 seconds spends 120. A still image spends 24 credits. You see the number before you start. If the clip fails, those credits come back.

faq.q: Which shapes can a clip use?
faq.a: Use 9:16 for a phone feed, 1:1 for a square, 16:9 for a wide page, and 4:3 or 3:4 when the page asks for them.
Avoid before-and-after bodies, medical outcomes, and dosage text inside the image. Show the product in a routine, and write the claims where you can check them.

faq.q: Can I start from a product link and make more than one version?
faq.a: Yes. Paste the product page, or send that link from your own shop through the API. Ask for a short script and pick an AI avatar. Make a few versions, including one in another language, and trim the clip in the editor before you export.

reviews.h2: How Wellness Brands Switch to AI Ads
reviews.lead: Example ways wellness sellers use one product photo. These are not quotes, and they are not health claims.

items.d: They upload a front-label photo and ask for the bottle next to fruit on a table. Dosage stays in the approved listing text.
A mat photo becomes hands unrolling it in a bright room. The scene stops there. It does not show a fitness result.
The same tin photo makes a square photo and a 10-second pour, then the tin is set down. That clip spends 40 credits.
They ask for the bottle in an open gym bag, and they leave out any line about what the drink does.
They compare the words on the bottle in the result with the real label. Dose and offers stay out of the picture.
If a preview implies a body change or a medical effect, they discard it and describe only the routine.

items.t: A link, then a short script
items.d: They paste the product page. Or they send that link from their own shop software (the API). They ask for a short routine script. The spoken line leaves out the dose.
They pick a person the tool creates for the breakfast scene. Then they make a second version of that same person. Neither clip shows a body change.
They choose a voice, or a short sample of their own. They check the captions, pick a music track, and trim the clip in the editor before export.
They make the breakfast clip again in a second language from the same photo. Approved claims stay in the listing, not in the picture.
They type the routine in the text box and keep a few versions. They send the one they want to TikTok, Facebook, or Instagram. A 10-second clip spends 40 credits.
